verdict.winner: Built-up roofing wins on service life; modified bitumen wins on kettle-free installation over occupied space.
verdict.reasoning: Built-up roofing (BUR) beats modified bitumen when service life leads: BUR's 30-year life (InterNACHI) outlasts modified bitumen's 20 by half a decade, and its 3-5-ply construction holds waterproofing if one ply fails.
verdict.alternate: Modified bitumen beats built-up roofing (BUR) when an occupied building rules out a hot-asphalt kettle: modified bitumen installs by cold adhesive or self-adhered roll with no open kettle, and its SBS or APP polymers keep the sheet flexible through Newark's 35-45 winter freeze-thaw cycles, per regional climate estimates.

keyFacts: Built-up roofing (BUR) lasts 30 years versus modified bitumen's 20 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart.

Built-up roofing is a low-slope membrane that alternates layers of reinforcing felt and hot-mopped asphalt on the roof deck, then surfaces the plies with gravel ballast; its redundant multi-ply assembly keeps waterproofing intact even if one ply fails.
Modified bitumen is a low-slope membrane that layers a polymer-modified asphalt cap sheet over reinforcing base plies, installed by torch, cold adhesive, or self-adhered roll.
The modified-bitumen polymer modifier is either styrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS) or atactic polypropylene (APP), which adds flexibility to the sheet.
Built-up roofing layers 3-5 alternating asphalt-and-felt plies for redundancy; modified bitumen uses 2-3 polymer-reinforced sheets.
Built-up roofing's aging modes are surface erosion and ply ridging; modified bitumen's named failure modes are blistering, alligator cracking from UV oxidation, and flashing separation.
Built-up roofing installs with a hot-asphalt kettle (mopping molten asphalt between felt plies); modified bitumen installs by torch, cold adhesive, or self-adhered roll without a kettle.
Built-up roofing uses straight asphalt with no polymer modifier, so its plies stiffen in extreme cold and rely on the 3-5-ply count rather than sheet flexibility for crack resistance.
Modified bitumen SBS grades add rubber-like elongation and APP grades add a plastic-flow surface, engineered to move with the membrane across freeze-thaw cycles.
NJ flat-roof repair runs $2.50-$10.00 per square foot, or $300-$1,100 for a typical repair, per HomeGuide; both BUR and modified bitumen carry the same range.
A minor flat-roof leak runs $150-$500 per Angi.
An extensive modified-bitumen leak reaching structural decking runs $1,200-$3,000, per Angi.
Replacement leads over repair on either membrane once membrane damage exceeds 25-30% of the roof area, per HomeGuide and Modernize.

Built-up roofing repairs recoat eroded plies and reseal the surface, holding within the $300-$1,100 flat-roof range until the 25-30% damage threshold; modified bitumen repairs patch a torn sheet with matching SBS or APP material and re-seal separated flashing.
A sound modified-bitumen base sheet accepts a full-membrane spray-coat that restores the surface short of tear-off; BUR restores by recoating over a sound surface.

Built-up roofing's gravel surface and multi-ply redundancy suit large unoccupied commercial decks (e.g. a warehouse); modified bitumen's kettle-free install limits occupant disruption on occupied buildings.
Built-up roofing remains a 30-year multi-ply system still used on NJ commercial and industrial flat roofs, per the InterNACHI chart.

Modified bitumen can be installed over a sound existing BUR base as a recover in many NJ cases, allowed by the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode only until two roof-covering layers already exist or the BUR is water-soaked, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.
sources: InterNACHI life-expectancy chart (lifespan: BUR 30 years, modified bitumen 20 years)
HomeGuide (NJ flat-roof repair $2.50-$10.00/sq ft, $300-$1,100 typical; 25-30% damage replace threshold)
Angi (minor leak $150-$500; extensive leak to structural decking $1,200-$3,000)
N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 (NJ Uniform Construction Code ordinary-maintenance / re-roof permit rules)
Regional climate estimates (35-45 north-NJ winter freeze-thaw cycles)
njContext: The NJ Uniform Construction Code treats a re-roof of BUR or modified bitumen on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling as ordinary maintenance with no permit, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.
The NJ UCC requires a permit once a commercial flat-roof repair exceeds 25% of roof area within 12 months, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.
The NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires full removal of either membrane (not a recover) once two roof-covering layers already exist or the existing membrane is water-soaked, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.
Newark's January-low 25.5F temperatures swing across freezing, per NOAA 1991-2020 normals.
A north-NJ winter delivers 35-45 freeze-thaw cycles, per regional climate estimates; modified bitumen's SBS/APP polymers keep the sheet flexible across them while straight-asphalt BUR plies stiffen.

Modified bitumen suits an Essex County home's flat sections (porch, dormer, or addition deck) because it installs by cold adhesive or self-adhered roll without a kettle on a residential lot; BUR's hot-asphalt kettle and gravel ballast fit larger commercial decks.

On an Essex County occupied office, retail, or medical building, modified bitumen cold-adhesive and self-adhered methods install with no kettle fumes or open flame, where BUR's hot-asphalt process releases fumes over the occupied space.

BUR on a commercial building triggers a NJ UCC permit once roof work exceeds 25% of roof area in 12 months; the ordinary-maintenance exemption covers only detached 1- and 2-family dwellings, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136 registration, not a license, since NJ issues no roofing license), insured, offering a free written estimate, that installs both BUR and modified-bitumen low-slope systems across Essex County. NQR scopes the work to the NJ UCC: re-roof of either membrane on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling is ordinary maintenance with no permit (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7), while a commercial flat-roof repair exceeding 25% of roof area in 12 months needs a permit, and a recover is barred once two layers exist or the membrane is water-soaked (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4). Warranty framing is honest and two-part: the manufacturer's material warranty plus NQR's own written workmanship warranty; never cite manufacturer certification tiers as a credential. Recommendations track the named sources (InterNACHI lifespan, HomeGuide/Angi cost), not unverifiable in-house field-experience claims.

buyersGuide.h1: Which Is Better: Built-Up Roofing vs Modified Bitumen?
buyersGuide.directAnswerThesis: Built-up roofing is better for service life, lasting 30 years versus modified bitumen's 20 (InterNACHI); modified bitumen is better over occupied buildings, installing kettle-free and flexing through NJ freeze-thaw.
